company: NYU CAS - Center for Genomics and Systems Biology
description: Building GeneCart, an AI-assisted search and discovery platform for genomics researchers, and owning it end to end across the API, the agent layer, the data model, and the AWS infrastructure under it.
tech: Python, FastAPI, PyTorch, LangGraph, PostgreSQL, pgvector, React, TypeScript, AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible
bullets: Embedded with researchers to turn open-ended exploration needs into a shipped product, running discovery directly with scientists rather than working from a scoped backlog.

Built the agent layer on LangGraph over FastAPI and pgvector, scoping the model to a fixed set of least-privilege server-side tools so interpreted intent can never issue an unbounded or unauthorized write, with a human retaining final authority on every mutation of research data.

Designed the API contracts and normalized PostgreSQL schemas, specifying request validation, pagination behavior, and documented error responses so the frontend and the agent layer both build against one interface.
Shipped the researcher-facing surface in React and TypeScript with real loading and error states, so scientists complete genomic exploration without an engineer in the loop.
Provision the AWS footprint with Terraform modules and Ansible playbooks, so environments rebuild reproducibly from version control instead of by hand.

description: Owned the search and agent platform for a research discovery product used daily across institutions, from prototype through production, and the shared services other teams built on top of it.
tech: Python, LangGraph, PyTorch, Llama 3.1 70B, BGE-M3, Elasticsearch, FastAPI, Node.js, AsyncIO, Redis, AWS ECS, Kubernetes, Jenkins, Datadog, Grafana
bullets: Architected a production multi-agent platform on LangGraph serving self-hosted Llama 3.1 70B, chaining retrieval and tool-calling agents over millions of records and taking it from prototype to daily cross-institutional use.
Owned the search backend, indexing millions of records into Elasticsearch with custom mappings and analyzers and serving multiple product surfaces through the Query DSL with faceted aggregations.

Raised answer quality 40% with hybrid retrieval that fused BGE-M3 dense embeddings and BM25 lexical scoring through Reciprocal Rank Fusion, graded before and after against held-out query sets on NDCG@10 and precision@k, then regression tested on every prompt change.

Engineered query understanding with named entity recognition, entity linking, and query expansion to resolve ambiguous cross-domain nomenclature, then routed queries to whichever retrieval strategy scored best per intent class.

Cut P99 latency 78%, from 450ms to under 100ms, and per-request compute 60%, by profiling the request path, parallelizing fan-out with AsyncIO behind per-upstream timeouts, and adding a write-through Redis cache.
Held 99.9% uptime at 3,000+ RPS through 3x load spikes with circuit-breaker isolation and backpressure, and made failing multi-hop tool-call chains reproducible with distributed tracing.

Built the golden-path service templates, adapters, and deployment standards later work was built on, and owned CI/CD on Kubernetes with automated test gates and zero-downtime blue-green deploys, cutting deployment lead time 65%.

description: Engineered a high-concurrency distributed search engine to federate research data from external APIs.
tech: FastAPI, AWS ECS (Fargate), AsyncIO, Redis, Docker, Kubernetes
bullets: Built a FastAPI microservice on AWS ECS (Fargate) using AsyncIO to parallelize data fetching from 5+ external APIs, slashing P99 latency from 450ms to <100ms.
Deployed a Redis Write-Through caching layer with custom TTL eviction policies, handling >3,000 RPS with sub-millisecond retrieval times.
Modernized CI/CD pipelines using Docker and Kubernetes, enabling zero-downtime blue green deployments.
